item.title: Iran War Live Updates: As Attacks Rattle Markets, Trump Seeks to Reassure Americans
item.summary: President Trump, speaking in the Oval Office, said he would do whatever was necessary to lower oil prices, even as new strikes on energy sites in the Gulf drove the price of oil to new highs.

item.title: The Iran War’s Economic Threat to Europe and Asia
item.summary: Inflation and its consequences for growth are a growing concern for countries where memories of the 2022 energy crisis are fresh.

item.title: Trump and Iran Dominate the Agenda as Europe’s Leaders Meet. Here Are 4 Things to Know.
item.summary: A gathering in Brussels was meant to concentrate on jump-starting the E.U. economy. Instead, the fallout of the war in the Middle East is front and center.

item.title: A Lebanese Cafe on the Edge of Destruction
item.summary: Near the center of Beirut, one image captures the aftermath of an Israeli strike.

item.title: Trump Jokes About Pearl Harbor in Meeting With Japan’s Leader
item.summary: Breaking a taboo, President Trump needled Japan’s prime minister about the World War II attack, as she widened her eyes and appeared to take a deep breath in the Oval Office.

item.title: U.K. Advisers Sent to U.S. to Help Develop Options to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: The move comes after President Trump sharply criticized Prime Minister Keir Starmer for not supporting his initial military strikes on Iran.

item.title: Israeli Officials Said U.S. Was Told about South Pars Attack
item.summary: President Trump first said the United States “knew nothing” about an attack on the gas field in Iran, which sent global oil and gas prices soaring. He then said he cautioned Israel against it.

item.title: The Soldier Who Came Back From the Dead
item.summary: Told that Nazar Daletskyi had died, his Ukrainian family buried what they thought were his remains. He turned up three years later in a prisoner-of-war exchange.

item.title: 2 Men Charged With Spying for Iran on Jewish Institutions in UK
item.summary: The men, both Iranian citizens, are accused of conducting surveillance on several Jewish institutions and community buildings in London.

item.title: Pakistan Pauses Afghanistan Airstrikes for Eid
item.summary: At least 143 people were killed in a Pakistani airstrike that hit a drug rehabilitation facility in Kabul on Monday, according to a top U.N. official.
